key_insight: CaRE-KD makes knowledge distillation confidence-aware by switching divergence direction and rejecting unreliable teacher updates when the teacher is less certain than the student.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical way to distill smaller LLMs that are better calibrated and more robust across reasoning, code, and alignment tasks without blindly copying noisy teacher outputs.
method: Token-level CaRE-Divergence adaptively switches between Forward KL and Reverse KL based on teacher–student confidence.
Batch-level Revival suppresses updates when the teacher is epistemically less certain than the student.
The framework is loss-agnostic and can plug into existing distillation objectives to filter unreliable supervision.
evidence_signal: Across eight teacher–student pairs and eleven benchmarks, the method improved instruction following, code generation, and mathematical reasoning, including gains of up to +1.7 on GSM8k and +1.8 on CollegeMath.
watch_item: Confidence gating depends on reliable uncertainty estimation, so miscalibrated confidence scores could weaken the selective distillation behavior.
paper_title: Distilling What Matters: Confidence-Aware Selective Distillation for Large Language Models
